text:
ConocoPhillips fell slightly today after a sharp three-day rally that pushed the stock up 6.7% from Wednesday to Friday. The decline follows news on Sunday that the Trump administration has suspended duties on Russian goods and eased sanctions on Russian energy, which raised expectations of increased Russian crude supply hitting global markets—a headwind for oil prices and exploration-and-production companies like ConocoPhillips. Oil prices themselves slid on the same news, though the sell-off has been modest so far given the stock's substantial two-week gain.

The broader backdrop remains supportive for oil companies despite today's dip. US crude is still trading around $102 a barrel, and the actual cost to physically deliver oil to end-users is significantly higher due to surging tanker rates—meaning the economics for producers remain strong even if headline prices pull back. The recent three-day surge in the stock reflects earlier this week's sharp rally tied to Iran escalating attacks near the Strait of Hormuz, which had driven Brent crude above $110; today's drop is a partial retreat from those geopolitical premiums rather than a break in underlying fundamentals.
